statements.text: At step $3$ there are $73$ holes, because $H_{3} = H_{2} + R_{2} = 9 + 64$.
Old holes remain when the new centre holes are added.

stem: Javed builds a Sierpinski Carpet. After step $2$ he has $H_{2} = 9$ holes and $R_{2} = 64$ remaining squares. At the next step every remaining square gains one new centre hole, and old holes stay, so $H_{n+1} = H_{n} + R_{n}$.

teacher.key_rationale: H3=H2+R2=9+64=73 and old holes remain, so statements 2 and 3 are true; statement 1 wrongly treats remaining squares as the hole count. Hence 2 and 3 only.
